reviewed_against: 3GPP TS 23.401 sec 5.3.2 initial attach and default bearer establishment
3GPP TS 23.401 sec 5.3.5 detach and bearer release
3GPP TS 29.274 sec 7.1 GTP-C tunnel identity: TEID, address and path peer
3GPP TS 29.274 sec 7.2 GTPv2-C tunnel management messages including Delete Session
3GPP TS 29.281 sec 4.4 GTP-U TEID and receiving endpoint

evidence_classification_layers: TRANSACTION_CORRELATION_PROVED: the accepted MATCHED transaction binding with a reviewed correlation strength
CONTROL_PLANE_CONTEXT_IDENTIFIED: the hop-local context seeded and addressable through receiver-scoped F-TEID joining
ENDPOINT_ADVERTISEMENT_OBSERVED: the S1-U bearer endpoint advertised inside an accepted transaction
ALLOCATION_ACCEPTED_OBSERVED: the correlated allocation response carries an accepted message-scope Cause
BEARER_ASSOCIATION_ESTABLISHED: the endpoint's grouped bearer items are accepted and one item-scoped bearer identity is isolated
RELEASE_OUTCOME_ACCEPTED: the correlated release response carries an accepted message-scope Cause
GENERATION_CLOSURE_ESTABLISHED: the full chain plus candidate-set completeness supports one closure
context_establishment_requires: proved MATCHED allocation transaction with reviewed correlation strength
joinable hop-local control-plane F-TEID corroborated by the publishing message's own path
allocation outcome ACCEPTED from the correlated response's message-scope Cause only
a rejected or unresolved allocation outcome keeps the context as a diagnostic candidate that establishes nothing
bearer_association_requires: every grouped bearer item of the endpoint inside the owning context accepted
an item without a grouped bearer Cause falls back only to its own transaction's correlated response message Cause
flat unbound IE values are never assigned to any item by position
at least one grouped bearer-context item with a readable item-scoped bearer identity
at most one distinct item-scoped bearer identity per endpoint in the context
exactly one endpoint of the receiving role in the context
hop_classification_requires: each classifying F-TEID corroborated by the publishing message's own source and destination addresses
a relayed foreign-interface F-TEID alone yields INSUFFICIENT_HOP_EVIDENCE and never seeds a context
response-side hop evidence remains usable when the response's own direction corroborates it
identity_rules.receiver_side_teid_interpretation: a GTPv2-C header TEID is interpreted in the scope of its receiving control-plane endpoint and its GTP-C path peer; it is never a globally unique context identifier
identity_rules.relayed_fteid_policy: a control-plane F-TEID whose interface type is foreign to the hop (an S5/S8 PGW GTP-C F-TEID published by an S11 response) is bridge evidence only and never a join key; an F-TEID with TEID 0 is an address hint and never a join key

correlation_strength_policy.STRONG: eligible when every other gate passes
correlation_strength_policy.SUPPORTED: eligible when every other gate passes; published so the weaker corroboration stays visible

not_confirmed: a hop-local session context is a control-plane grouping, not proof of a complete EPC session
an endpoint correspondence never establishes cross-interface session identity by itself
a numerically equal TEID, EBI or sequence number is never an identity bridge
a release bound to a control-plane context does not by itself close a bearer generation
an accepted release outcome stays unchanged whatever the session binding resolves to
the exact instant user-plane forwarding stopped is never proven by a release response
no subscriber identity, APN name or assigned PDN address is read or published
no complete EPC session or bearer state machine is implemented
